# Introduction

`persephone3` provides multiple ways to visualize seasonal adjustment results. The plotting functions return interactive HTML widgets using `dygraphs` and `plotly` (see the `plotEngine` argument of the plot functions).

**Note:** The appearance of plots depends on whether `run()` has been called. Before running, only the raw time series is available. After `run()`, additional components (seasonally adjusted, trend-cycle, forecasts) become accessible.

## Plot size and mouse position

The interactive plots fill the plot pane of RStudio and Positron: a plot shown on its own gets the whole pane and is redrawn whenever the pane is resized, so a small pane gives a small plot and nothing has to be scrolled. In a report or vignette (and in the dashboards) the plots keep their own size, `options(persephone3.plotFill = FALSE)` switches the filling off, and `options(persephone3.plotHeight = 300)` (together with `persephone3.plotWidth`) gives a plot a size of its own instead.

Moving the mouse over a plot draws a vertical line at its position and shows the values of all plotted series at this date together; no dots are drawn at the hovered points of the individual series. The series the cursor is on is highlighted: it is drawn bold while the other series fade. In the plotly plots a click on a series fixes its highlighting; a click on another series moves it, and a click on empty space shows all series with equal strength again.

```{r setup-example, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(persephone3)

# Create seasonal adjustment object
obj <- perX13(AirPassengers, "rsa1")
```

# Default Plot Method

The default `plot()` method creates an interactive time series plot using `dygraphs`. You can zoom into specific periods and hover to see exact values.

```{r default-plot}
# Plot before running - shows raw data only
plot(obj, drawPoints = TRUE)
```

After running the model, the plot includes additional components and forecasts:

```{r run-before-plot}
obj$run()

# Plot after running - shows SA, trend, and forecast
plot(obj, drawPoints = TRUE, showOutliers = FALSE)
```

# Seasonal and Irregular Components

Visualize the seasonal and irregular components with `plotSeasIrrCal()`:

```{r plot-seas-irr}
plotSeasIrrCal(obj)
```

# Residual Analysis

`plotResiduals()` creates interactive diagnostic plots using `plotly`. You can examine autocorrelation (ACF) or partial autocorrelation (PACF):

```{r plot-residuals}
# ACF of residuals
plotResiduals(obj, which = "acf")

# PACF of residuals
plotResiduals(obj, which = "pacf")
```

# Plotly Engine

For alternative styling, the plot functions with an interactive engine accept
`plotEngine = "plotly"` (see `?plot`):

```{r plotly-plot, eval = FALSE}
plot(obj, plotEngine = "plotly")
plotSeasIrrCal(obj, plotEngine = "plotly")  # no range slider below the plot
plotSiRatios(obj)  # plotly is the default engine here
plotSpectrum(obj)  # plotly is the default engine here
```

# Spectral Plots in Panels

`plotSpectrum()` overlays the spectra of all requested series types in one
plot (`layout = "overplot"`, the default) or places every combination of
plot type and series type in a framed panel of its own (`layout =
"panels"`). The panels form a square-ish grid of equally wide columns
and every panel keeps the height:width ratio of a single plot:

```{r plot-spectrum-panels}
plotSpectrum(obj, tsType = c("original", "sa", "irregular"),
             layout = "panels")
```

# Plotly Integration

Some methods return `plotly` objects directly, allowing further customization:

```{r plotly-custom}
# ACF plot with plotly
p <- plotResiduals(obj, which = "acf")
p  # The plotly object can be further customized
```
